title: A Push for Peace
subtitle: Inside the briefcase lies irrefutable evidence that peace is possible.

items.text: A Push for Peace
The stranger studies Marsha again.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty, and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Pardon?

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: You possess remarkable self-control. A trait seldom seen.
A hint of approval, odd and unspoken, leaves Marsha unsure how to react.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: My thanks. But I have a question.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: As I have one for you.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Why did you kill the colonel?

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Answer me likewise: why did you protect him?
Marsha gestures toward the slope to the row of crude headstones filling the ridge.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: We're trying to end the war.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: And I, as well.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: You seem to mourn the dead, but you don't realize how far you've set us back? We were nearing a ceasefire.
Petals from pale flowers tumble by in the dry wind.
Sentinel leans forward, gently shielding the flowers from the wind with her cloak.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Six years, and the war rages still. Do you think ending bloodshed is as simple as to say: 'tis done? Have you any mind of the mission the Foundation pursues here?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: We know it won't be simple.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Yet each side was open to negotiation. That's why they sent ...

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Heh.
The chuckle is wry and dark.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: You placed false hope on Hirschfelder. You invited a wolf into a bed of lambs.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: You think his death to be the spark of a reignited war, but, even if I had stayed my hand from him, your plans would have been for naught.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: The Manus scheme and the wicked prosper.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Manus Vindictae. You know of their plans? Then, you're claiming that Hirschfelder was a Manus?
She lets the question linger long enough to feel unanswered, then the sniper begins.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: He is not one of those devils. He is only one tool of many.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: The Manus offer the gifts of Mammon and Asmodeus: greed and destruction. Hirschfelder was tempted by their technologies and became a willing servant in their schemes.
A groan rises up from the horizon, the sound of distant artillery drumming, throbbing like the heartbeat of a wounded beast.
She raises a second finger.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: But others serve them unknowing, affected by an arcane skill which clouds their eyes in red mists, driven to blood and glory as a starving dog is to the hunt.
Her eyes shift to the stiff outline of a soldier she knows as Charon.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Your commander, Eberhard Braun, bears that mist.
It takes a moment for the words to find some impact. When he speaks again, there seems to be a change in his voice.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Then will you see that death comes to him, as you did Hirschfelder?

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: That is not yet certain. I do not kill without purpose.
Charon does not seem to find a reply, his mask concealing any trace of emotion.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: What you just said about the Manus ... Can you confirm any of it?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: The Foundation could make use of any intelligence you have. We may be able to save these peace talks.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: But we will need proof.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: All is vain. There is nothing new under the sun.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: When I told my commander about the Manus, all I received for my effort was scorn. Their eyes were not satisfied with seeing, nor their ears with hearing. Kings and generals yet still turn a blind eye to the suffering.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: If they had a shred of the light of God within them, they would never have pursued this war.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: As for the Foundation ... That which is crooked cannot be made straight, and what is wanting cannot be numbered. I have no faith in them.
She looks away, pulling her cloak tighter.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: That is all I have to say.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Spare him.
Charon speaks, the change in his voice now more acute, more vivid, and more personal.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Eberhard Braun. I need you to spare his life.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Neither mercy nor vengeance is mine to give.

"It is officially 1920. I wonder at other people's impressions of this war; from what I've seen, 
there are two contrasting views—though in various forms—one of heroism and the other, sadness."

"There is one truth which I have found bridges both of these visions, 
despite how cruel it may sound—'This war is the prelude of a new era.'"

"I have to believe that ... Because if this death and destruction so unparalleled in history does not herald change, 
then there is no hope for humanity."

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: How bleak.
The leader of the "XII" stands on the streets of Montpaix, looking over where Colonel Hirschfelder was killed.
By the time he arrives, all other military forces have withdrawn. Only the Foundation remains on site to guard the ruins of the town.

items.speaker: "Officer"
items.text: Blackbird, give me a hand.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: As soon as I finish my bread, Beagle.
His team has already begun shoring up the town's defenses. Their line pulled back to just a corner of the street.

items.speaker: Foundation Security Staff
items.text: There are 122 armed personnel available at your disposal, sir. 23 of them are arcanists.

items.speaker: Foundation Security Staff
items.text: I've brought you their profiles.
He takes the personnel file from the security staff member, eyes shifting toward the makeshift HQ flying the Foundation flag.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Right then. I'll read through these. Now get back to your position. I need eyes on our command post.

items.speaker: Foundation Security Staff
items.text: Yes, sir.
The staff member walks away. And in the same moment, a curiously armored field medic approaches.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Marsha, is it?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: You recognize me, Mr. Creius?

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: I read your report on my way here. You're the one that encountered our sniper. Twice now, I hear.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Correct. I have some additional details about my encounters. The first is that I appear to have been followed out into the forest the first time. I was warned on my device just after the shooting.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Never mind that. What about the other thing?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: That doesn't concern you? Fine. The other thing is that I have reason to believe our sniper is a Gargoyle.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: A Gargoyle?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: There are records of Gargoyles participating in this war as part of arcane skill response units.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: They're able to petrify their bodies at will, making them immune to small-caliber arms, and I believe they're able to render themselves undetectable.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Sounds as if you've fought them before.
The assumption pierces her more cleanly than any bullet, but she forces the emotion down, giving an answer as truthful as she can bear.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: You could say that.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: It would go far to explain how she managed to enter Montpaix without being noticed. I'll have to ask HQ to send us a counter-arcanum device.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: She shot the colonel, but then slipped out, leaving our own agents unharmed. We can't be sure of anything, but we can't rule out that she may possess reliable intel about the Manus.
Rushed footsteps interrupt Creius's thoughts.
Mr. Creius?
The newcomer is obviously out of place—the sort of well-dressed that usually comes with fanfare.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: I am Georg Kramer from the Inter-Factional Committee. I've come on behalf of the parliament to start another round of negotiation with the Foundation.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Didn't you get the message? The parley has been canceled, Mr. Kramer. Seems there's no more room for negotiations.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: My job now is to investigate the possible involvement of Manus Vindictae.
The visitor steps forward. Though he lowers his voice, a trace of urgency and excitement leaks through.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: Precisely what I'm here for, sir.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: We received a warning from the Foundation that Manus Vindictae has infiltrated our armed forces and is attempting to usurp our rightful authority. I am worried this may be true.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: I do not intend to lie, sir; Germany lies on the verge of total collapse. Both politically and rationally speaking, we have no reason to continue this war.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: Yet it seems our army command is out of control; they are determined to drive this war to its bitter end regardless of the misery and death they're causing. And I have reason to believe the Manus are behind it.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: I take it Army Command is not aware of your visit then, Mr. Kramer.
The observation is sharp, to the point, and, quite obviously, correct.
Perhaps to reassert some authority, the man arches his shoulders back, adopting an almost regal pose.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: I represent the majority of the parliament, sir, as well as the office of the Imperial Chancellor.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: We are united now. All we need is some hard evidence.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: If it can be proven to His Imperial Majesty and to the chancellor that Army Command has been infiltrated by this Manus cult, I am certain we will have the authority to end this.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: So, you're asking me to share the result of my investigation to root out the rotten apples in your army.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: I am, sir. We'll do everything we can to restart the parley once we take control.
His head bows deep and serious, though the sudden winter wind tosses his hair and collar out of place.
He pulls in a deep breath.

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: And we're willing to reach a ceasefire on certain conditions. I assure you I'm not just saying this because of my stance ...

items.speaker: Georg
items.text: For the sake of my country and its people, this war must be stopped.
